paras: This Thursday, a classic Thanksgiving dinner for ten people will cost fifty-eight dollars and sixty-three cents.
That's from the American Farm Bureau's yearly survey. And it's up more than six percent from last year.
The biggest villain? It's sitting in the middle of your table. The turkey. A sixteen-pound turkey now costs about twenty-three sixty-eight. That's up ten percent in just one year.
But here's the weird part. Dinner is still cheaper than in twenty twenty-two, when the same meal hit a record sixty-four dollars.
And where you live matters. In the South, it's about fifty-four dollars. In the Northeast, about sixty-one fifty.
Add extras like ham, potatoes and green beans, and the bill jumps to almost eighty-two dollars.
Want to pay less? Some grocery stores sell turkeys at a huge discount the week of Thanksgiving. Some even give one away free when you spend a minimum amount.
Why? Because the turkey gets you in the door. They make their money on everything else you grab.
So buy the cheap turkey, and stick to your list.
What will your Thanksgiving dinner cost this year? Tell me in the comments.
